Feature: GPIO Positive-Edge Interrupt Enable and Validation (All Pads)
Test Description: Validate that enabling positive-edge interrupts on all GPIO pads results in an interrupt for each pad upon a rising edge. Configure per-pin control registers for positive-edge detection, enable the group interrupt mask for all pads, generate rising edges, verify interrupt status, then clear and confirm deassertion.
Meta Test Description: The test configures platform and system interrupt routing for the GPIO block, programs all per-pin control registers (starting at the base per-pin register and continuing by word stride) for positive-edge interrupt detection, and enables the group interrupt mask for all pads. A stimulus source is toggled from low to high to create a positive (rising) edge on enabled pads. The main loop waits for the default interrupt handler to fire. In the ISR, the handler confirms the per-pin status/edge indicators, checks the group interrupt status bit(s) for the active pad(s), clears the raw status and verifies that the group status deasserts. The test iterates across all enabled pads (or handles all pad bits indicated by the group status) and records any timeout or mismatch as a failure before reporting the final result.
Remarks: Ensure platform interrupts for the GPIO instance are enabled and cleared during service. Configure positive-edge selection prior to enabling group masks. The external stimulus must be capable of generating rising edges on the targeted pads. Verify group status is cleared after raw status clear.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the platform and system interrupts for the GPIO instance. 2) Initialize the external stimulus to a known low level. 3) Configure all per‑pin GPIO control registers for positive‑edge interrupt detection. 4) Enable the group interrupt mask for all pads. 5) Generate a rising edge on the enabled pads using the external stimulus. 6) Observe that an interrupt is triggered and service it via the ISR. 7) In ISR processing, verify that the per‑pin and group interrupt status reflect the positive‑edge event. 8) Clear the raw interrupt status and confirm the group status deasserts. 9) Repeat/iterate to cover all pads that are enabled. 10) Declare PASS if all pads generate and clear interrupts as expected; otherwise FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: Initialization: test_err=0. Enable platform IRQ(s) for the GPIO instance (e.g., GIC IRQ ID associated with GPIO0/1) and enable system interrupt routing in the SoC interrupt enable register. Configure all per-pin control registers (base_per_pin + i*4 for i over enabled pads) to select positive-edge interrupt mode; insert small waits if required. Enable the group interrupt mask register to allow all pad bits (e.g., write all-ones mask). Stimulus: drive external stimulus low, then transition to high to create positive edges (either one pad at a time using (1<<i) or all pads together via a full mask). Event handling: set a pending flag, then wait with timeout for ISR entry. In Default_IRQHandler: clear the pending flag; optionally restore stimulus to idle; read the active pad’s per-pin control/status register and check that input/edge status indicates a positive-edge event; read the group interrupt status register and confirm the corresponding bit(s) are set; write to the raw interrupt status clear register to clear the event bit(s); re-read the group status to confirm deassertion (zero). Also write the SoC raw status clear register and clear the GIC IRQ. Error accounting: any timeout waiting for ISR, missing status bit, or failure to clear increments test_err. Completion: finish(test_err).
Impacted Registers: GPIO GP0 per-pin control registers (GPIO_8 .. GPIO_39), GPIO GP0 Group Interrupt Enable 1, GPIO GP0 Group Interrupt Status 1, GPIO Raw Interrupt Status Clear 1, LSS SYSREG Interrupt Enable 1, LSS SYSREG Raw Status Clear 1
Meta Impacted Registers: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 (+ i*4), MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each enabled pad triggers a positive-edge interrupt upon a rising transition, the corresponding group status bit sets, and after clearing the raw status the group status reads zero. Any timeout or mismatch = FAIL.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Timeout: if ISR not observed within the configured timeout after generating a rising edge, mark FAIL. Per‑pin check: per‑pin status indicates positive‑edge event when read post‑ISR. Group status set: group status register shows the bit(s) corresponding to the active pad(s). Clear and verify: writing the raw status clear register deasserts the group status to zero. Final: finish(0) if no errors; otherwise finish(non‑zero).
